chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Fadl Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dirhams that are carried (as currency). He said: 'If you spend what is permissible among the people of the city, there is no problem; and if you spend what is not permissible among the people of the city, then there is [a problem].'
ai.seo_question: What determines the validity of currency in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Shia legal principle of *urf* (social convention) in determining the validity of currency, linking monetary value to communal acceptance rather than intrinsic worth. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, who adapted to the economic realities of their time by validating coins based on their circulation and trust within the local market. This establishes a flexible framework for *fiqh al-nuqud* (jurisprudence of money) that remains relevant in modern economic contexts.
